(i) Bag-of-Local-Features models are surprisingly competitive in ImageNet classification, (ii) the Bag-of-Local Features model is a good proxy for the decision strategy of state-of-the-art DNNs, and (iii) the Bag-of-local-features model is considerably easier to understand than DNNs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether DNNs are qualitatively different from previous models.
the following question: How much can we explain and understand the decision process in a DNN by replacing the complex architecture with a simple bag-of-local-features model?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bag-of-features approach, despite its simplicity, is a surprisingly good model of the decisions made by DNNs.
DNNs are better than BoF models but not qualitatively different.
BagNet-16x16 is a good approximation to ResNet-50.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNNs are surprisingly similar to bag-of-local-features models in terms of performance, feature sensitivity and decision strategy.
BagNets are surprisingly good at ImageNet classification, that their decisions are easy to understand and that they behave similar to state of the art DNNs.
BagNets are not only surprisingly accurate but also surprisingly similar to deep neural networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decision strategy of DNNs on ImageNet can be surprisingly easily approximated by a simple BoF classifier, which is much easier to analyse.
the BagNet is an excellent tool to understand how DNNs make their decisions.
DNNs can be replaced by simple bag-of-feature models without sacrificing performance, while at the same time providing much more intuitive explanations for their decisions.
